issues.title: Waste collected before contractor arrival has no supported later-handover operation
issues.actual: The screen requires weighing/recording each category per area at collection, and recording the consignment at later contractor handover. POST permits collection-only rows, but the bundle/reference/search expose only POST/GET /infection/waste. A confirmed synthetic collection waste_id=1 (0.25kg NonRisk,2026-11-05) remains vendor_id/manifest/disposal null and handed_over_kg=0. There is no supported operation to attach later handover to this existing collection. PUT /infection/waste/1 returns404 NOT_FOUND. A new collection POST would count the same weight again, so frontend does not offer that workaround.
issues.expected: Per waste_log_ops rule:889ac3e40b ('Weigh each category’s bags per area at collection; record the contractor’s consignment note at handover'), support an idempotent later-handover operation referencing existing waste IDs (or a documented batch/partial handover workflow) without recording collection weight again. Specify permission, validation, conflict/recovery semantics and totals, then update bundles/types/workflow/test plan. If the intended workflow differs, document how to satisfy both collection-time recording and later consignment safely.

issues.response: Confirmed, and thank you for refusing to record the same weight twice: that was the right call. A waste record could take its consignment note only at the collection; nothing attached one later. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) POST /infection/waste/handover {waste_ids, vendor_id, manifest_number, disposal, handed_over_on (default today)} attaches one consignment note to the collections it covers, each handed over whole and once: the weight is never entered again. Its permission is the one that records waste (infection.waste.record), and both waste_log and waste_log_ops list it (one new endpoint item each on your checklist; no approved rule was reworded). Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry after a lost answer gets the same answer; sent again without it, the collections are refused. (2) The answer: the contractor, the note, the disposal, the day, weight_kg (the sum of the collections it covers) and the records. (3) Refusals: WASTE_HANDED_OVER (409, new: a collection already carries a note; details.waste_id, manifest_number, handed_over_on; it is final), REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND (details.field waste_ids with the unknown ids, or vendor_id), VALIDATION_ERROR (a handover in the future, or before a collection's day). (4) GET /infection/waste?awaiting_handover=true lists the collections no note covers yet, however old: the screen's handover picker. Each record now carries handed_over_on and handed_over_by_name (null while it waits), and the totals' handed_over_kg follow. (5) The database keeps it so: a collection never changes once recorded, and a consignment note is final once attached; one given at the collection (POST /infection/waste with vendor_id) is dated that day. A collection is handed over whole, never in part: bags that leave on different days are weighed as separate collections. The infection-control playbook, both screens' bundles and the description of POST /infection/waste say so. This update changes the migrations, so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your synthetic waste_id 1 is gone. To check it: as demo.ops record two synthetic collections without a contractor; GET /infection/waste?awaiting_handover=true lists them; POST /infection/waste/handover with both, a contractor from GET /finance/vendors?vendor_type=Contractor and a synthetic note: 200, weight_kg their sum; the same again without a key: 409 WASTE_HANDED_OVER; the totals' handed_over_kg equal their weight_kg.

issues.build: index-O27FYLR1.js; base 6cd3b4d plus audited equipment implementation
issues.response: Confirmed, and thank you for checking that the route works and that no duplicate was open: it is exactly a catalogue gap. Both equipment screens take vendor ids (supplier_vendor_id and service_vendor_id on PUT /facility/equipment/{asset_id}; vendor_id on a contractor's plan and visit) but did not list the directory they come from. Checking every screen the same way found three more forms in the same position: equipment requisitions (an option's vendor_id), the operations console (a work order's contractor, a utility bill's provider) and lab administration (PUT /lab/contractor contractor_vendor_id). From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) GET /finance/vendors is listed by equipment_maintenance, equipment_maintenance_ops, equipment_requisitions, ops_console and lab_admin, so get_screen_bundle, generate_typescript(kind=screen) and screen_test_plan of each include it. (2) The route has a description now: the directory every vendor picker reads, open to any logged-in user; filter by vendor_type (Contractor, EquipmentSupplier, UtilityProvider, ...) and offer the active ones (is_active); finance adds a vendor with POST /finance/vendors. vendor_type is a typed value list now, so an unknown type answers 422 VALIDATION_ERROR instead of an empty list. (3) Each vendor field of those forms names the directory in its description, as category_id names GET /ops/utility-categories. (4) The playbooks facility-compliance-equipment-drills, facility-and-it and laboratory-and-radiology say where each vendor is picked. (5) A backend test fails on any screen whose form takes a vendor id without listing GET /finance/vendors. No response field changed. Your checklist gains one endpoint item on each of those five screens; no approved rule was reworded. This build also carries the fix of #53, which changes the migrations, so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays). To check it: get_screen_bundle for equipment_maintenance and equipment_maintenance_ops lists GET /finance/vendors; generate_typescript(kind=screen, name=equipment_maintenance) has its function; as demo.maintenance GET /finance/vendors?vendor_type=Contractor answers the contractors, and ?vendor_type=Plumber answers 422. (6) This build goes further (decision 62, commit 7429acf): checking every screen for the same gap found 86 screens whose forms take other ids from lists their bundles did not name (departments, wards, staff, patients, stays, medicines and their batches, assets, theatres and more). Each now lists its directory, each field's description names it, and the test of (5) covers every such id, except those the backend wrote down with a reason (the record the form is opened on, or an id the owner chose to leave without a picker). GET /staff/lookup also answers user_id (null without a login) for the fields that name a user; the bed matrix (its wards, without patient names), GET /ot/theaters and GET /ops/assets (without the purchase cost and date) are open to the screens that pick from them; the Quality Officer may read the formulary; GET /lab/reagents/{reagent_id}/batches is new. Your checklist gains 139 more items (138 endpoints and one rule on report_incident), none reworded. The update note lists every screen and what your app should do.
